sources: dossier=Required behaviors line 19 ('both row-disposition branches (durable promote / delete) bump the counters') and line 21 ('the durable-Commit contract forbids undoing a promotion'), artifact-tier, corroborated by the doc's own invariant 5 (row preserved by promote); doc=invariant 3 said termination follows from deletes; code=terminal_decision.go:114-127 shows only Source==OwnershipBail deletes, every other Abandon promotes via promoteHandleState
note: Doc's own invariant 5 and the dossier both establish that terminal children are promoted and preserved, not deleted; invariant 3's delete-based termination argument was internally inconsistent with that. Rewrote invariant 3 to ground termination in depth-boundedness plus the promote/skip-non-active mechanism.

sources: dossier=silent on this specific mechanism; design corpus=cancel-siblings.md's Multi-supervisor scope section states cross-supervisor children 'continue to natural completion; each Commit / Abandon bumps the parent counter independently' while a different supervisor holds the parent -- direct contradiction of an actor-restricted reading; code=child_execution.go:295 passes parent.HolderSupervisorID (the row's own value) into BumpChildOutcomeCount, and the takeover branch at :393-400 reassigns holdership only after settlement, not before
note: claim-tree.md's invariant 4 wording overstated the guard as restricting bumps to 'the supervisor that holds the parent'; cancel-siblings.md (an adjacent, non-accused design doc) already documents cross-supervisor settlement bumping the counter as intended. Rewrote invariant 4 to describe the guard as targeting the row's current holder with reassignment-on-takeover, matching the corroborating doc.

sources: dossier=Net position line 11 ('a parent claim auto-terminals only after all its sub-claims are terminal') and Required behaviors line 17 (2026-05-15, artifact, 'parent auto-terminals only after all sub-claims are terminal'); doc=Definition said resolving a child 'fires the parent's own terminal' with no gate; code=child_execution.go:317-334 returns early (after the counter bump) if any parent holder or child claim-handle row is still active
note: The dossier explicitly requires the all-terminal gate in two independent places; the doc's Definition omitted it, which would mislead a reader into expecting every child resolution to fire the parent terminal. Added the gating condition to the Definition's second paragraph.

sources: dossier=Net position line 12 describes descendant-cancel as an unconditional top-down cascade on any abandon, distinct from the strict+cancel_siblings-gated sibling-cancel; doc=claim-tree.md Boundaries said the descendant-cancel walk is 'used by concept:cancel-siblings' while cancel-siblings.md's own Boundaries separately claims 'the recursive descendant cascade' as owned by cancel-siblings, both docs claiming the same mechanism
note: Per the dossier, descendant-cancel is a general tree-integrity mechanism that fires regardless of cancel-siblings policy, so it belongs to claim-tree, not cancel-siblings. Rewrote claim-tree.md's Boundaries to own the descendant-cancel walk outright and describe its unconditional trigger, and moved the cancel-siblings citation to the boundary line describing what claim-tree does NOT own (the proactive sibling-cancel layered on top). cancel-siblings.md's Boundaries line still claims 'the recursive descendant cascade' as owned there too -- that file is out of scope for this edit but should be reconciled to stop double-claiming ownership of the same walker.

sources: dossier=Net position line 12 ('a claim's abandon recursively force-abandons descendant claims (descendant-cancel)' as unconditional, distinct from the strict+cancel_siblings-gated sibling-cancel); doc=Boundaries described the descendant-cancel walk as 'used by concept:cancel-siblings'; code=terminal_decision.go:114-119 fires cancelDescendantClaims on every IsAbandon() outcome ungated, while cancelInFlightSiblings alone is gated on AggregationKindStrict + CancelSiblings
note: Same underlying boundary-line fix as row 236 resolves this: rewrote the Boundaries 'Owns' clause to state the descendant-cancel walk fires unconditionally on any Abandon, independent of aggregation policy or the cancel-siblings setting.

sources: dossier=Required behaviors line 19 ('both row-disposition branches (durable promote / delete) bump the counters') acknowledges promote as the general branch and delete as the other (bail) branch; doc=invariant 1 said the descendant-cancel walk fires 'BEFORE the parent's own delete...for the Abandon case'; code=terminal_decision.go:121-127 deletes only when Source==OwnershipBail, every other abandon promotes to state=abandoned
note: The general Abandon case never deletes the parent row at all; only the ownership-bail source does. Rewrote invariant 1 to say the walk fires before the parent's own terminal resolution, naming both possible dispositions (promote to abandoned, or delete under ownership-bail).

sources: dossier=silent on this specific qualification; design corpus=cancel-siblings.md's Multi-supervisor scope (load-bearing) section documents the claimant-guard filter as deliberate ('a supervisor cannot release claims held by a different supervisor'); code=terminal_decision_cancel.go:130-132 skips descendants where HolderSupervisorID != args.SupervisorID
note: cancel-siblings.md already documents this filter as intentional for its own sibling walk; claim-tree.md's invariant 1 stated the orphan-avoidance property unqualified. Added the same supervisor-scope qualification to invariant 1, citing cancel-siblings.md's multi-supervisor scope section.

sources: dossier=Net position lines 11-12 name the two walks distinctly (bottom-up parent-resolution vs top-down descendant-cancel); doc=invariant 3 said 'the recursive walker' as if there were one, packing two different termination arguments for the two walks named in Boundaries
note: Folded into the same invariant-3 rewrite as row 39: the new text explicitly says 'both recursive walks' terminate by depth-bound, then names the descendant-cancel walk specifically for its extra frontier-shrinking argument, removing the ambiguous singular 'the recursive walker'.

sources: dossier=Required behaviors line 20 describes the descendant walk as cleanup ('cancels grandchildren before each row's own delete') rather than an aggregation-relevant path; design corpus=cancel-siblings.md invariant 3 describes the descendant walk firing 'inside the recursive resolution frame' of an already-resolving ancestor; code=terminal_decision_cancel.go:176 sets ParentClaimHandleID: nil for descendant-cancelled children, and terminal_decision.go:137-139 skips SettleFromFanoutChild (and therefore BumpChildOutcomeCount) when that field is nil
note: Descendant-cancelled children's immediate parent is itself mid-resolution in the same walk, so there is no live parent aggregation to feed -- the code's omission of the counter bump there is correct, not a bug. Doc's invariant 5 overgeneralized 'terminal children...participate in the parent's aggregation counter' to cover this case; qualified it to natural settlement and sibling-cancellation only.

sources: design corpus=auto-terminal.md's own What-it-is section scopes the concept to 'the end of a held claim's holding-subgraph' and its Boundaries explicitly excludes 'the active-terminal (non-held) branch that also routes through the same unified resolution engine (see terminal-resolution for the unified spine)'; doc=claim-tree.md Definition labelled the parent-resolution walk 'the auto-terminal recursion'; code=terminal_decision.go:140 invokes SettleFromFanoutChild from ResolveClaimHandleTerminal for all sources, including ActiveTerminal (non-held)
note: auto-terminal.md itself disclaims ownership of the non-held branch and points readers at terminal-resolution for the unified engine; claim-tree.md's own citation pointed at the wrong neighbor. Renamed the walk to 'the parent-resolution walk, part of the unified terminal-resolution engine' and added concept:terminal-resolution to Adjacent.

sources: dossier=silent; doc=invariant 2 said tree shape is 'enforced structurally (a single parent pointer per row)'; code=migrations/001-initial.sql:418 declares parent_claim_handle_id with no CHECK/trigger preventing cycles, acyclicity holds only because runner_subclaim.go always inserts children with a freshly generated id pointing at a pre-existing parent (never rewires an existing row)
note: This is a factual mechanism-description error, not a contested design intent: a single parent pointer only guarantees at-most-one-parent, not acyclicity. Rewrote invariant 2 to attribute acyclicity (and thus the tree shape) to insert-time discipline rather than a structural DB constraint.
